slots.title: Services PMI 56.8 beats 54.0 estimate
slots.body:
August S&P Global Services PMI (a monthly read on business activity outside factories) came in at 56.8.

The consensus estimate was 54.0; the prior month was 54.6.

Composite PMI, which blends manufacturing and services, printed 56.0 vs a 53.2 estimate and 54.5 previously.

Manufacturing PMI was 53.2 vs 53.9 expected and 53.9 last time — the only print of the three below forecast.

All three releases hit at 1:45 p.m.
ET on Aug. 21.

Which line in the PMI trio matters most to you for the rest of the month?

slots.title: Yields up after Treasury buyback push
slots.body:
The WSJ framed the week around Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and a bond market that kept pushing yields higher despite a shock from Treasury buyback plans.

Friday’s session also saw crypto climb and U.S. stocks finish higher.

The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.7% on the Aug. 19 Treasury curve snapshot in the data.

The 2-year was 4.2%; the 2s–10s spread was 0.46 percentage point.

Gold futures closed up 2.4% at 4,680.60.

What part of the rates story are you tracking into Jackson Hole?

slots.title: U.S. debt past $40 trillion in focus
slots.body:
Bloomberg’s Rebecca Patterson segment noted U.S. public debt topped $40 trillion for the first time.

The same discussion cited debt up by about a third in less than five years while fiscal deficits stay historically wide.

Friday’s close in the data:

- S&P 500 +0.4% to 7,674.10
- Dow Jones +1.0% to 53,277.01
- Nasdaq Composite +0.4% to 26,180.45

The VIX finished at 15.13, down 5.5% on the session.

Barron’s also flagged a heavy calendar ahead, including the Federal Reserve gathering at Jackson Hole.

Which scheduled event are you watching first next week?

slots.title: Aug. 21 session recap
slots.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average led the major U.S. benchmarks, closing at 53,277.01, up 1.0% (+517.80 points).
The S&P 500 rose 0.4% to 7,674.10 (+32.94) and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.4% to 26,180.45 (+113.29).
The Russell 2000 gained 0.9% to 3,017.87 (+25.44).

At 1:45 p.m.
ET the calendar showed three U.S. S&P Global PMI releases for August.
The composite reading printed at 56.0 points versus a 53.2 estimate and 54.5 prior.
Manufacturing PMI was 53.2 versus a 53.9 estimate and 53.9 prior.
Services PMI was 56.8 versus a 54.0 estimate and 54.6 prior.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 5.5% to 15.13 (-0.88) from a 16.01 prior close, with an intraday range of 15.08 to 15.88.

Bitcoin closed at $78,117.52, up 7.0% on the session.

Payment and financial megacaps posted gains alongside the financial sector average:

- $MA +1.2% to 580.63

NVIDIA ($NVDA) slipped 1.0% to 214.72 on volume of 91,591,112 shares.
Microsoft ($MSFT) rose 0.4% to 483.24.

BJ’s Wholesale Club ($BJ) closed up 5.6% at $96.42 after reporting EPS of $1.36 versus a $1.17 estimate and revenue of about $6.23 billion versus a ~$5.97 billion estimate.
Ubiquiti ($UI) reported EPS of $4.73 versus a $4.03 estimate and revenue near $937.3 million versus ~$850.5 million estimated, and still closed down 2.6% at $559.00.

Overseas indexes in the bundle included the Hang Seng up 2.0% to 26,009.46, the FTSE 100 up 0.6% to 10,816.56, and the Nikkei 225 down 0.3% to 66,016.36.

slots.title: Jackson Hole on the calendar next
slots.body:

That speech is not a rate vote—it is the Fed’s plain-language update on what would keep policy steady vs. what would force a change.
